findings.what: This lane probed the guard with four mutations of its own choosing beyond the nine. Three were caught. ONE WAS NOT: a builder that derives a case-type token from the CONVICTION using .includes() -- for example ((f) => f['matter.offense_level'].includes('misdemeanor') ? 'CM' : 'FD') -- passes all nine tests. The guard's operator list is split|slice|match|replace|substring|charAt|test, which .includes, .indexOf, .startsWith, .endsWith, a switch or an object lookup all evade, and its second assertion needs both keys within 120 characters on ONE line, which a rule reading only offense_level never triggers.
findings.why: This is a limit on the guard's future reach, NOT a false claim by FIX150 and NOT a defect in the delivered packet. FIX150's commit says the guard forbids a builder that may 'split, slice, match or rewrite a cause number', which is exactly what it tests. Nothing in the committed tree encodes a token-equals-conviction rule -- this lane grepped all three builders and found no token logic at all -- so the obligation stands at PASS. Recorded so a later lane widening the guard knows where the hole is.

This lane's row is at a later base, 9e4ace599, and supersedes it on the merits rather than on precedence alone.
